persona.bio: Dani, 34, runs a mobile dog grooming van on her own in a suburb of Atlanta. Six or seven dogs a day. Clients book by text, and she answers the same questions all day: prices by breed, how long it takes, whether she does nails only, how to reschedule. She sends reminder texts the night before, writes a short note after each groom about matting or skin, and posts before and after photos on Instagram. Bookings live in a paper diary and her phone's calendar. She has never used AI.

steps.note: I run my own mobile dog grooming van, and I work from my phone. I write to dog owners by text, mostly about bookings and reminders. My tone is warm, friendly and short, like a quick message from someone who knows their dog. Keep replies to a few sentences. Use plain words and no fancy phrases. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, times, addresses or what a dog needs. If something is missing, put it in square brackets so I can fill it in. I read everything before I send it.

steps.title: Your owner reminder texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your reminder texts now live on your phone’s keyboard, each one a few letters away. You type a short shortcut and the full text appears, then you change the name or the time. That fits your day better because you send these many times a day, from the van, with one hand free.

items: Hi! Just a reminder [dog’s name] is booked for [day] at [time]. The van will be in your driveway. Please keep [him or her] in the house until I arrive. See you then!
Hi! I’m on my way and should be there around [time]. Please keep [dog’s name] inside until I get there. See you soon!
Hi! Quick reminder that [dog’s name] has a groom coming up on [day and time]. Could you reply to let me know that still works?
Hi! I’m running a little behind and now expect to be there around [new time]. Thank you for your patience!
Hi! I’ve arrived and the van is parked at your place. You can bring [dog’s name] out when you’re ready.
Hi! [dog’s name] is all done and looks great. [Short note about the groom]. Thank you, see you next time!

steps.title: Your booking messages, saved once on your phone

Hi! I don’t have anything open on [day]. I can do [first option] or [second option]. Which suits you better?
Hi! No problem, let’s move [dog’s name] to [new day and time]. Does that work for you?
Hi! Thanks for letting me know. I’ve cancelled [day and time] for [dog’s name]. Message me whenever you’d like to rebook.

safeUse: Never type an owner’s full name, phone number or home address into a chat tool. Use square brackets or a role like “an owner”.
Keep your replies to saved text on your phone’s keyboard, with brackets for the parts that change, so private details stay in your own messages.
Never put payment details or card numbers into a chat tool.
When a dog has a skin or health concern, describe it in general words and leave out the owner’s details. Check anything about a dog’s health against what you know and trust before it goes out.
Read every message before you send it, and fill in every square bracket.

design.today: You send these many times a day, each one typed from scratch. The last one you wrote was a reminder to the owner of Biscuit about Thursday at 10am, with the van in the driveway and the dog kept indoors.
design.newWay: Your reminder wording is saved once on your phone, so each text is a few letters away instead of typed from scratch. You type a short shortcut, fill in the dog's name, day and time, read it and send it yourself. The wording stays the same every time and you keep your own voice.

steps.goal: Get Claude ready on your phone so you have a helper for writing your saved replies.
Paste in your Biscuit reminder and ask for a few versions with gaps for dog name, day and time, such as a first reminder, a day before reminder and a running late note.
Pick the reminder versions you like best and trim them to the ones you send most.
Save each reminder so it is a few letters away in your text messages.
Try the shortcuts on your next real reminders and adjust the wording until it sounds like you.

Save the booking replies so each one is a few letters away in your text messages.
Check your free slots in the calendar before you fill the day and time into a booking reply.
